0x0807DDB8.review: The only aligned Thumb pointer to this callback is registered at 0x080792DA in slot 3 of 0x03002730. The scheduler dispatches eight slots at 0x08070588. State zero copies the byte at menu offset 0x561 to 0xC1F. Original stores at 0x08076F6E, 0x080765FA, 0x08076FCA and 0x08077068 write 0, 1, 2 and 3 to offset 0x561. The callback calls 0x0807DC24 before reloading the menu pointer and choice. The live menu object must retain a choice below four when the byte is used at 0x0807DE64. Coverage of other writers and preservation of that value are unproved runtime premises.

0x080D8E00.review: The sole callback registration at 0x080D97D0 allocates 0x16C bytes and phase 0 derives counts 1, 2, or 4 from the mode. Ten of eleven direct spawner calls use constant BG and coordinate and fit all eight scroll table slots. At 0x080EA44E, mode 2 and coordinate 0 use min(map layer bytes 0x02007F40 and 0x02007F41). The active map must select a first register at most four here, and its callback payload must retain its initialized count and selector throughout phase 0x100. 0x0801E204 initializes (1,0), 0x0801D2B8 saves the pair and substitutes enabled layers (3,2), and 0x0801D494 restores the pair. Preservation of that map state by other writers is an unproved runtime premise. The loop advances one table index per channel.

0x080E3E84.review: payload->selector (+1) is written only in this function's phase 0, from descriptor->selector (+0x16). The sole spawner, func_080E4054 (callback literal at 0x080E41A0, no other reference), passes its own mode byte (+3) there. func_080E4054 phase 0 is the only writer of that byte and stores 0, 1 (selector 0x65) or 2 (selector 0x109), so the index is 0..2, within the 3-entry tables data_08149C88/data_08149C94.

0x080D9170.review: payload+8/+9 are written only in phase 0, as u8 copies of descriptor+0x14/+0x16. The only spawner, func_080D989C (the sole reference to this callback), stores its u8 arguments there. Its only caller, func_080EA938 at 0x080EAA34, passes the constants first=3 and second=0, so the index is always (3<<1)|0 = 6 < 8, within the 8-entry tables data_08149AD4/data_08149AF4. The only other access to the payload, func_080D9B38, writes +0 only.

0x0801E2A4.review: The only static writers of g_state_02007F40 bytes 0..4 are as follows. func_0801E204 sets 1,0,2,3 and index 1 via func_0801E098, whose only caller it is. func_0801D2B8 saves bytes 0/1 to +0x22C/+0x22D and sets them to 3/2. func_0801D494 restores them from +0x22C/+0x22D, which only func_0801D2B8 writes. Every stored value is therefore 0..3, the BG numbers the func_080034B8 family takes. The callees between the loads (func_081443FC into the stack copies, func_08003A74/func_08003A80, which are pure, and func_080034B8/08003508/08003558, which write only the 0x03000940 shadow registers) never store to 0x02007F40. Unlisted setters at 0x0801E54C/0x0801E558 have no BL or pointer reference. This rules out static writers only: a store through a computed pointer or a bulk copy over 0x02007F40 is not excluded beyond the literal and store scans, which found none except the init clear that func_0801E204 overwrites.

0x080E317C.review: payload->index (+2) is written only in this function's phase 0 (strb at 0x080E31B8, the only store to +2), as descriptor byte +0x14 minus 0x62. The callback's only references are entries 12 and 13 of the {callback, payload size} table data_08395280 (words at 0x083952E0/0x083952E8; no other aligned word 0x080E317D and no BL to 0x080E317C in the ROM). That table is addressed by func_080D3508 (literal at 0x080D35BC) and by func_080D3818 (literal at 0x080D3854, 0x08395320 = data_08395280 + 0xA0). For ids above 0x155 func_080D3508 selects entry id - 0x156, stores the u16 id at descriptor +0x14 (strh at 0x080D3518, descriptor at sp+4) and passes that descriptor to func_08005954, which copies its 28 bytes, zeroes only the phase halfword and runs phase 0 once before setting the task phase to 0x100. The 0x159 override at 0x080D356E affects entry 3 only. So through func_080D3508 this callback runs only for ids 0x162 and 0x163; the low byte at +0x14 is 0x62 or 0x63 and the index is 0 or 1, within the 2-byte tables data_08149C84/data_08149C86. func_080D3818 stores its u16 id the same way (strh at 0x080D3824) but selects entry id - 0x157 (0x08395320 + 8*(id - 0x16B)), so it would reach this callback for ids 0x163 and 0x164, and 0x164 would store 2. Its only references are three BLs: 0x081251EA and 0x081253B0 in func_08124FD0 pass an id in 0x16A..0x269, and 0x08121470 in func_0812130C, to which nothing in the ROM refers, passes an id in 0x170..0x19D. This rules out static writers only: a store through a computed pointer into the task payload is not excluded beyond the literal and BL scans.

0x081171CC.review: payload+1 (direction) is stored at 0x0811729E in phase 0x100 as the constant 0, 1, 2 or 3 picked by the x/tile_x and y/tile_z compares, and that store precedes both loads on every path: 0x081172A2 follows it directly, 0x081172C6 follows only the call to func_080D5CC0, whose arguments (data_08502560, the frame byte, the s16 x/y values, constants) do not include the payload. No other path reaches either load, so the index is 0..3, within the 4-byte arrays frames/flags at sp+0x10/sp+0x14. The callback's only reference is the literal 0x081174DC in the spawner func_08117320, which keeps the task handles only for func_080E0570 to poll and free.

0x08111D50.review: payload->counter (+0, u16) starts at zero: func_08005B6C passes the 0x10-byte payload size to func_08005954, which allocates size + 0x1C bytes and clears all of them (func_0814224C, bx r2 to the IWRAM zero-fill at 0x03005E78 named by the ROM word 0x0836D4B8) before the phase-0 call; the payload is task+0x18..+0x28. Phase 0 writes only +8. The only store to +0 is the increment strh at 0x08111DC6 in phase 0x100, after the load at 0x08111D9E, and it is followed by 'if counter > 4 then phase = 2'. The runner func_08005A24 passes the saved phase back each frame and nothing sets 0x100 again, so the five phase-0x100 calls load 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and the index is below 5, within the 5-entry offsets copy of 0x08149F40. The callback's only reference is the literal 0x081122A8 in the spawner func_081120CC (no BL, no other word), which keeps the handle at its own payload+0x10 only for func_080E051C to poll and free.

0x081031AC.review: payload->index (+3) is written only in this function's phase 0 (strb at 0x08103244, the only store to +3), as descriptor byte +0x14. The callback's only reference is the literal at 0x08103A84 inside func_081037B0 (the one pc-relative load of it is at 0x08103A52; no other aligned word 0x081031AD and no BL to 0x081031AC in the ROM). That loop (entered only at 0x08103A34 with r4=0, back-edge only from 0x08103A6E, `cmp r4,#2; bls`) stores its u8 counter with strh at descriptor +0x14 (0x08103A46) and passes the descriptor to func_08005B6C, whose func_08005954 copies its 28 bytes, zeroes only the phase halfword and runs phase 0 once before setting the task phase to 0x100, so the index is 0, 1 or 2, within the 3-byte stack copies of data_08149DF0/F3/F6/F9 (each filled by func_081443FC with n=3). 0x080D4D58.review: The index is the low byte of r0 (lsls/lsrs #24 at 0x080D4D5C/0x080D4D5E). The only references to this function are four BLs and no literal or branch (no word 0x080D4D59 or 0x080D4D58 and no B/Bcc to it anywhere in the ROM): 0x081177BA and 0x081177C2 in func_08117784, and 0x0811AD36 and 0x0811AD3E in func_0811ACF4. At all four the first argument is a byte that func_0801E610 has just copied out of g_state_02007F40 into the caller's frame: byte 0 (at sp) for the first call and byte 1 (at sp+1) for the second. Only the first func_080D4D58 call, which does not write the caller's frame, lies between that copy and the second load. The static writers of those two bytes are the ones the 0x0801E2A4 entry lists. func_0801E204 sets 1 and 0 (strb at 0x0801E216/0x0801E21A) right after the init clear at 0x0801A084. func_0801D2B8, which addresses the block as 0x02008168 - 0x228 (literals 0x0801D480/0x0801D484), saves them to +0x22C/+0x22D (0x0801D32A..0x0801D330) and sets 3 and 2 (strb at 0x0801D396/0x0801D3FE). func_0801D494 restores them from +0x22C/+0x22D (strb at 0x0801D4C2/0x0801D4CA); those two save bytes are written only by func_0801D2B8 and are zeroed by the init clear (0x450 bytes from 0x02007F40), so the restore yields 0 or a saved 0..3. The other users of the 0x02008168 - 0x228 alias (func_08019E84, func_0801D818, func_0801D8E8, func_0801D938) only read through it or store the halfword at +0x2C, the unlisted setters at 0x0801E54C/0x0801E558 have no BL or pointer reference, and the one call found that passes the block's address on (0x0801ACB6, through func_0801B7F8 to func_0801AF08) stores the halfword at +0x2C only. Every stored value is therefore 0..3, within the 4-entry stack copy of data_08149AB4 (the BG0CNT..BG3CNT shadows 0x03000942..0x03000948). This rules out static writers only: a store through a computed pointer or a bulk copy over 0x02007F40 is not excluded beyond the literal, BL and base-alias scans, nor is an overrun of a neighbouring buffer such as the LZ77 decompression to 0x02007CB0 in func_0801F438, whose length comes from the data header.

0x080DE33C.review: The index is u8(r2) (lsls/lsrs #24 at 0x080DE34A/0x080DE34C) into the 2-halfword stack copy (4-byte copy, 0x080DE352) of g_object_08149B70. The function has seven BLs and no literal or branch reference: 0x080DDE12, 0x080DE8F4 and 0x080DEC56 pass the constant 0, and 0x080DF886, 0x080FA366 and 0x08100616 pass the constant 1 (a movs r2 directly before the bl, no branch lands between). The seventh, 0x080DB0B4 in func_080DB00C, passes payload+9, which phase 0 stores only at 0x080DB08A as a copy of byte 9 of the structure descriptor +4 points to. That call is guarded by the copy of byte 7 of the same structure (ldrb [r7,#7]; cmp #0 at 0x080DB0A4, the bne at 0x080DB0A8 being the only way in), so it runs only if that byte is non-zero. func_080DB00C is referenced only by two literal words. The one at 0x080DC21C belongs to func_080DC1E8, which builds the structure on its own stack with byte 7 = 0 (0x080DC1F6/0x080DC202) whatever its arguments. The one at 0x080DB5B4 belongs to func_080DB540 phase 0x100, which passes its own payload+0x18. Those 20 bytes are written only in func_080DB540 phase 0, by the call at 0x080DB584 through the pointer word 0x0836D4BC to the Thumb routine at 0x03005EE8; func_08002768 installs that routine from ROM 0x08A38A9C (image 0x08A38A2C..0x08A38ADC copied to 0x03005E78), and it copies exactly r2 = 20 bytes from r1, the structure func_080DB540's descriptor +4 points to, to r0 and stores nothing else. func_080DB540's other payload stores are at +4, +5, +8, +0xC, +0x10 and +0x14. Its only references are the literal words at 0x080DC2A8 and 0x080DC2EC, in func_080DC268 and func_080DC2AC, which both build that structure with byte 7 = 0 (0x080DC284 and 0x080DC2CE); the three callers of func_080DC268 keep the returned task only for func_080DBA5C to poll and free, and func_080DC2AC is not called from code (the only matching BL encoding, at 0x081F1AAA, lies in data). func_08005954 runs phase 0 once, synchronously, from its copy of the descriptor and then sets the task phase to 0x100, and func_080DB540 never returns to phase 0x100. So the call at 0x080DB0B4 is never reached and every reachable call passes 0 or 1, within the 2-entry table. This rules out static spawners only: a computed callback address, a store through a computed pointer into the task payload, a task phase reset by external code, or the installed IWRAM routine being overwritten is not excluded beyond the literal and BL scans.

0x080D9488.review: Both loads read the callback descriptor in phase 0: u16 at +0x14 (0x080D94D2) is the background and u16 at +0x16 (0x080D94D6) the coordinate, and (coordinate<<24 | background<<25) >> 22 is the byte offset 4*(background*2 + coordinate) into the two 8-word stack copies of data_08149AD4 (sp+0) and data_08149AF4 (sp+0x20) in the 0x40-byte frame. The only reference to this callback is the literal word at 0x080D9938 in func_080D9914 (no BL or branch to 0x080D9488 and no other word 0x080D9489 or 0x080D9488 anywhere in the ROM), which stores its u8 arguments at descriptor +0x14 and +0x16 (strh at 0x080D9924/0x080D9928) and passes it to func_08005B6C/func_08005954, which copies the 28-byte descriptor and runs phase 0 once, synchronously, before setting the task phase to 0x100. func_080D9914 has six callers and no literal reference, all passing constants set directly before the bl: 0x080ED564 (2,0), 0x080EF584 (3,1), 0x080EF7F8 (2,0), 0x080FD150 (3,0), 0x0811239E (2,1) and 0x08119402 (3,0). The index is therefore 4..7 and the byte offset 16..28, below 29, so each 4-byte load ends within its 8-entry (32-byte) table. The later phases never read the descriptor fields. This rules out static callers only: a computed callback address or a task phase reset to 0 by external code is not excluded beyond the literal, BL and branch scans.

0x080D9350.review: The index is s16 descriptor+0x14 (ldrsh at 0x080D9396), read only in phase 0 from the 28-byte descriptor copy that func_08005954 passes to the single, synchronous phase-0 call before setting the task phase to 0x100. The only reference to this callback is the literal word at 0x080D9910 in func_080D98D4 (no BL or branch to 0x080D9350 and no other word 0x080D9351 or 0x080D9350 anywhere in the ROM), which stores u8(r0) at descriptor +0x14 (lsls/lsrs #24 at 0x080D98DC/0x080D98DE, strh at 0x080D98E4), so the value is 0..255 and never negative. func_080D98D4 has six callers and no literal reference, all passing a constant first argument set by a movs r0 in the straight-line setup before the bl: 0x080E539E (2), 0x080EAEE6 (2), 0x080EECC4 (2), 0x080F24DA (2), 0x080F291C (3) and 0x0811B806 (2). The index is therefore 2 or 3, within the 4-entry (16-byte) stack copy of data_08149B14 (the BG0VOFS..BG3VOFS registers 0x04000012..0x0400001E) at sp+8 of the 0x18-byte frame. The other phases never read the field. This rules out static callers only: a computed callback address or a task phase reset to 0 by external code is not excluded beyond the literal, BL and branch scans.

0x0810533C.review: payload->index (+2) is written only in this function's phase 0 (strb at 0x081053A6, the only store to +2), as the low byte of descriptor +0x14 plus 0x16 (ldrb at 0x081053A2, the only read of that field, adds at 0x081053A4), truncated to u8. The callback's only references are entries 233..237 of the 8-byte {callback, payload size, flags} table at 0x083947D8 (words at 0x08394F20/28/30/38/40; no other word 0x0810533D or 0x0810533C at any alignment and no BL or branch to 0x0810533C in the ROM). The table (0x083947D8..0x083954B8) is addressed only by func_080D3508 (literals at 0x080D355C/0x080D35C8, and 0x080D35BC for its second part 0x08395280), func_080D3B98 (0x080D3BC4, reads byte +6 of an entry only) and func_080D3818 (0x080D3854, base 0x08395320); the other words with a value inside it (0x0839493E at 0x0815C728 and three unaligned byte runs at 0x0858DC29, 0x0858F69F and 0x085CF2D2) lie in data, are not entry-aligned and are not addressed by a pc-relative load. func_080D3508 keeps its u16 id in r4, stores it at descriptor +0x14 (strh at 0x080D3518, descriptor at sp+4, not written again) and selects entry id - 1 from the same register (0x080D354C for ids up to 0x155, 0x080D3564 above; for id 0x159 it substitutes func_080E2398 at 0x080D356E), then passes the descriptor to func_08005954, which copies its 28 bytes, zeroes only the phase halfword and runs phase 0 once before setting the task phase to 0x100. So through func_080D3508 this callback runs only for ids 0xEA..0xEE, whatever its 48 callers pass; the byte at +0x14 is then 0xEA..0xEE and the stored index is 0..4. func_080D3818 stores its u16 id the same way (strh at 0x080D3824) but selects entry id - 2 (0x08395320 + 8*(id - 0x16B)), so it would reach this callback for ids 0xEB..0xEF, and 0xEF would store 5. Its only references are three BLs. 0x081251EA and 0x081253B0 in func_08124FD0 pass the word at sp+0, written only at 0x08124FE0 and 0x08125006 as u16(u16(r0) + 0x16B); func_08124FD0's only reference is the BL at 0x08123986 in func_0812397C, which passes u16(ldrb - 1), so that id is 0x16A..0x269. The third, 0x08121470, is in func_0812130C, to which nothing in the ROM refers (no BL, no branch, no word 0x0812130D or 0x0812130C at any alignment); it passes the u16 at +2 of the record its payload counter selects in the 16-byte-record table 0x083A7A34, the records 0..0x4A that its end test (cmp #0x4a at 0x081218D4) covers hold opcode 0 only with ids 0x170..0x19D, and the counter moves only by +1 or by the +3/+7 skips of the opcode 5 records, which land inside that range. So no call of func_080D3818 selects this callback and the index is 0..4, within the 5-byte stack arrays rows (phase 0) and bits (phase 0x103), both at sp+0x14 and each filled by func_081443FC with n=5 from ROM 0x08149E38 or 0x08149E3D before its load. The task runner func_08005A24 passes later phases a descriptor holding the phase only, and this function sets the phase to 0x101..0x104 or 2, never 0. The payload pointers it passes out (+4, +6, +8, +0xC, +0x18, +0x28) all point above +2; func_080D48DC, the one callee given a payload pointer in phase 0x103 before the load, writes only the three words at +0x28. This rules out static writers only: a store through a computed pointer into the task payload (callees receive the task handle as the parent of the tasks they spawn), a callback address built without a literal, a task phase reset to 0 by external code, or func_0812130C being reached with a counter outside 0..0x4A is not excluded beyond the literal, BL and branch scans.

0x081160E4.review: payload->kind (+0) is written only in this function's phase 0 (strb at 0x0811614E, the only store to +0), from byte +4 of the parameter block that descriptor+4 points to. The callback's only reference is the literal at 0x081164C4 in func_08116480, which builds that block on its own stack (strb of its u8 first argument at 0x08116498) and passes it to func_08005B6C; func_08005954 copies the 28-byte descriptor, zeroes only its phase and runs phase 0 once (call at 0x08005A08) before setting the task phase to 0x100, so the block is live while phase 0 reads it. func_08116480 has no literal reference and three BL callers, each passing a constant first argument: 0x08112AAC in func_08112A60 passes 1 (movs r0,#1 at 0x08112AA4), 0x08115D48 in func_08115CE4 passes 0 (0x08115D44) and 0x08118564 in func_08118500 passes 2 (0x08118560). The index is therefore 0..2 and the halfword offset 0..4, within the 3-entry halfword tables data_08149F60/data_08149F66 copied to the stack. 0x08114438.review: Both sites index with payload->counter (u16 at entry_R2+0), re-read at 0x08114790 and 0x081147A0 inside the block that is entered only by falling through the function's own guard at 0x08114774-0x08114778 (ldrh r0,[r7]; cmp r0,#4; bhi 0x081147C2; no branch in the function targets 0x0811477A..0x081147C0), so the guarded value is 0..4. Between the guard's load and the second re-read the only stores are the three strh of func_08011040 (bl at 0x0811478C; ROM 0x08011040..0x08011054 stores only through r1, r2 and r3, which are sp+0x28, sp+0x2A and sp+0x2C of this frame, set at 0x0811477E..0x0811478A, and it pushes only r4/lr) and the strh at 0x0811479E to sp+0x28; r7 is not written. The payload is not this frame: the callback's only reference is the literal word at 0x08115704 in func_08115560 (no BL to 0x08114438 and no other word 0x08114439 or 0x08114438 in the ROM), which passes it to func_08005B6C with payload size 0x80, and both callers of the callback, func_08005954 (phase 0) and the runner func_08005A24, pass r2 = task+0x18 of the block func_08007138 allocated from the task heap. The object func_08011040 reads (*payload->first, the word at the spawner's payload+0x10 that func_081141EC phase 0x100 sets) is only read. Both re-reads therefore return the guarded value and the index is below 5, within the 5-entry stack copies of the initialisers at 0x08149F4C (sp+0x10) and 0x08149F56 (sp+0x1C). Tasks run only from the loop of func_08005A24, none of whose 13 call sites is in the VBlank callback func_080004B0 or its direct callees, so no other task runs inside that window. This rules out synchronous writers only: an interrupt handler storing into this payload between 0x08114774 and 0x081147A0 is not excluded. The handler table at 0x0814942C holds two routines besides the bx lr stub 0x080027FC: the serial handler that func_08004AC0 copies from 0x080050C8 to 0x03002A00, whose ARM body (to 0x03002AF4) stores only into its own block at 0x030028A0, through the buffer pointers func_08004AC0 sets inside that block, and to the SIO registers; and the VBlank callback func_080004B0, whose callees (DMA request lists, OAM upload, effect-node list) take their destinations from RAM lists and were not traced exhaustively. The only two functions that store into the RAM copy of the table at 0x030008D0, func_08031698 and func_08089C84, install func_08031624, which stores only BLDCNT, and the empty func_0808A1E8. Nor is the disjointness of the heap block and the stack proved beyond the allocation path.

0x08136A10.review: The sole caller at 0x08136342 reaches this routine in title phase 7. The main three-item selection and the alternate selection wrap between 0 and 2 on input. The alternate selection originates from the two-bit saved mode; the three-item menu requires a valid saved mode (0..2). Each index is required in that range when the corresponding style byte is written. This is a runtime precondition, including after the alternate-mode callbacks.

0x0800CF08.review: 0x0800CF08 has no caller in this ROM: no Thumb BL, B, Bcc or ADR and no aligned ARM B or BL reaches it, and no 32-bit word at any byte offset equals 0x0800CF08 or 0x0800CF08|1 in the 0x08000000, 0x0A000000 or 0x0C000000 mirror. Its scanline callback func_0800D3BC is referenced only by the literal pools of the four creators 0x0800CF08, 0x0800CFC8, 0x0800D090, 0x0800D168 (0x0800CFC0, 0x0800D08C, 0x0800D164, 0x0800D238), and none of the four is referenced, so the load at 0x0800CF46 never executes and the row holds vacuously. The intended domain agrees with the bound: the index selects bg - 2 from data_08149820 = {0x04000020, 0x04000030}, the BG2 and BG3 affine parameter registers, and only BG2 and BG3 have affine registers, so bg is 2 or 3 and ((bg << 24) >> 22) - 8 is 0 or 4, below 5.
